signatures.docstring:
Extract all antibiotic prophylaxis intervention arms evaluated in the study, including placebo and no-antibiotic control arms, as a structured table with one row per arm.

Form Questions:
- interventions: "Extract ALL antibiotic prophylaxis arms (including placebo/no-antibiotic controls) evaluated in the study, with one row per arm."

This signature captures repeating arm-level data from randomised controlled trials of antibiotic prophylaxis. Each arm is described independently; no cross-arm aggregation is performed here. Arms include active antibiotic regimens of any duration as well as placebo or no-treatment controls.

input_fields.desc: Full markdown content of the clinical research paper from which antibiotic prophylaxis arm data will be extracted.
input_fields.name: markdown_content

output_fields.name: interventions
hints: Look in the Methods section under 'Interventions', 'Study Arms', 'Treatment Groups', or 'Randomisation'
CONSORT flow diagrams and baseline characteristics tables often list arm sizes
Dose and regimen details are typically in a dedicated 'Antibiotic Regimen' or 'Prophylaxis Protocol' subsection
Allergy substitution regimens may appear in footnotes, supplementary material, or a separate paragraph within the methods
rules: Extract EVERY arm including placebo and no-antibiotic control arms — do not omit any arm
Each arm occupies exactly one row; do not aggregate or merge arms
Use {"value": "NR", "source_text": "NR"} at the whole-field level only if the document contains no intervention arm data at all
For a missing value within an otherwise-present row, use {"value": "NR", "source_text": "NR"} for that cell
output_fields.description: All antibiotic prophylaxis arms evaluated in the study, including placebo and no-antibiotic control arms, with one row per arm and per-cell source grounding.

hints: Construct this label yourself from the arm_category you assign and the antibiotic_name you extract — it is not usually printed verbatim in the paper
Scan the methods section, CONSORT flow diagram, and treatment allocation tables to identify all distinct arms before assigning labels
For multi-drug combination arms, use the principal (first-listed or highest-dose) antibiotic as the main drug in the label
If the paper uses shorthand arm names (e.g. 'Group A', 'Arm 1'), map these to the structured label format rather than copying the shorthand
Ensure each arm in the same study has a unique label; if a collision occurs, add a parenthetical distinguishing detail derived from duration, dose, or route
rules: Label format must be exactly '<arm_category>, <antibiotic_name>' using the same arm_category value assigned in the arm_category field and the generic (INN) drug name from antibiotic_name
For placebo or no-antibiotic control arms, the label must be exactly 'placebo' — no category prefix
arm_category values to use in the label: 'single preoperative dose', 'short-term', 'long-term', or 'placebo'
No two arms within the same study may share an identical arm_label; append a parenthetical distinguishing detail if needed
Use only lowercase for the category and drug name portions of the label
Do not include dose, route, or frequency in the label unless needed to disambiguate a collision
subform_fields.field_description: Build a CONSISTENT label as '<regimen category>, <main antibiotic>', using the arm_category you assign and the principal drug — e.g. 'long-term, amoxicillin', 'short-term, penicillin G', 'single preoperative dose, clindamycin'. For placebo / no-antibiotic control arms use exactly 'placebo'. If two arms in the same study would get the same category+drug label, append a short distinguishing detail in parentheses (e.g. 'long-term, penicillin (2 days)' vs 'long-term, penicillin (2 days + 5 days oral)').

hints: Look in the methods, interventions, or treatment arms section for descriptions of when and how long antibiotics were given

Check the duration field and dose timing to determine the correct band: a single pre-incision dose → 'single preoperative dose'; total course ≤24 h (but more than one dose or extending into peri-operative period) → 'short-term'; course extending beyond 24 h post-surgery → 'long-term'
For control arms, check whether participants received placebo tablets/injections or simply no antibiotic — both map to 'placebo'
If the paper describes a regimen as 'prophylactic single dose' or 'preoperative antibiotic', classify as 'single preoperative dose' even if the paper does not use that exact phrase
When duration is ambiguous, use the dose timing and frequency fields to infer the band
rules: Must be exactly one of: 'single preoperative dose', 'short-term', 'long-term', 'placebo'
A single dose given only before incision is always 'single preoperative dose', never 'short-term', even though it is also <24 h
'short-term' applies only when the regimen extends beyond a single pre-incision dose but the total course is ≤24 h
'long-term' applies when the course continues >24 h after surgery, regardless of total number of doses
Both placebo-controlled arms and no-antibiotic control arms must be classified as 'placebo'
Do not use 'NR' — every arm must be classifiable from the duration and dose information available; if genuinely ambiguous, choose the closest category and note it in arm_label
subform_fields.field_description: Regimen-length band you classify yourself from the duration the paper describes for this arm. 'single preoperative dose' = one dose before incision only; 'short-term' = peri-operative course lasting ≤24 h; 'long-term' = course continuing >24 h after surgery; 'placebo' = placebo or no-antibiotic control arm. A single pre-incision dose is its own category even though it is also <24 h.

hints: Look in the Methods (Interventions) section, drug tables, or arm descriptions for the specific antibiotic name
Brand names (e.g. Augmentin, Dalacin) must be converted to their INN generic equivalents (e.g. amoxicillin-clavulanate, clindamycin)
For combination regimens, identify each individual drug and join with ' + ' (e.g. 'ampicillin + sulbactam')
Control arms labelled 'placebo', 'no treatment', 'no prophylaxis', or 'observation only' should be recorded as 'placebo' or 'no antibiotic' respectively
If the paper names only a drug class (e.g. 'a cephalosporin') without specifying the drug, use 'NR'
This field captures the drug name only — dose, route, frequency, and duration are captured in separate fields
rules: Use INN generic names only; never use brand names
For combination regimens, join drug names with ' + ' (e.g. 'amoxicillin + clavulanate')
For placebo or no-antibiotic control arms use exactly 'placebo' or 'no antibiotic' as appropriate
Use 'NR' if only a drug class is mentioned and no specific drug name is given
Do not include dose, route, frequency, or duration in this field — those are captured elsewhere
subform_fields.field_description: Generic name(s) of the antibiotic(s) used in this arm, or 'placebo' / 'no antibiotic' for control arms. Examples: 'amoxicillin', 'penicillin G', 'clindamycin', 'amoxicillin + placebo'. Convert brand names to generic (INN). For combination regimens join names with ' + '. Use 'NR' if only a drug class is reported and no specific name is given.

hints: Look in the Methods section under 'Interventions', 'Treatment', or 'Antibiotic regimen' for the arm already identified
Check dosing tables, regimen description paragraphs, and footnotes for each dose event in sequence
For multi-stage regimens (pre-op → intra-op → post-op), capture all stages in order
Route information may appear alongside dose; include it here only as part of the dose event string if it disambiguates timing (the route field captures the overall route separately)
If the paper describes a loading dose followed by maintenance doses, include both with their respective amounts and timing
rules: Copy dose amounts and units verbatim from the paper (e.g., '1 g', '500 mg', '2 MU'); do not convert or normalise units
List dose events in chronological administration order separated by commas: pre-operative → intra-operative → post-operative/maintenance
Include timing qualifiers as stated (e.g., 'at induction', '3 h post-op', 'every 8 h for 5 days')
Do NOT duplicate information already captured in the `frequency` or `duration` fields unless it is integral to describing a specific dose event
For placebo arms, record the dose of the placebo formulation if described (e.g., '1 g IV placebo at induction'); use 'placebo' if no dose quantity is given
Use 'NR' if the dose amount or units are not reported anywhere in the paper

examples.value: 1 g IV at induction, 500 mg IV at 3 h post-op, 500 mg PO every 8 h

subform_fields.field_description: Full dose(s) with units for the regimen, in administration order (pre-op / loading → intra-op → post-op / maintenance) exactly as the paper states. Include EVERY dose event and its timing. Example: '1 g IV at induction, 500 mg IV at 3 h post-op, 500 mg PO every 8 h'. Use 'NR' if the dose is not stated.

hints: Look in the methods/interventions section where the regimen for the identified arm is described
Route is often stated alongside dose and frequency in the arm description or in a summary table
If the dose field already contains route abbreviations (e.g. 'IV', 'PO', 'IM'), use those to determine the correct option
For multi-phase regimens (e.g. IV loading then oral continuation), select the combined option such as 'IV + oral'
rules: Must be exactly one of the allowed options: 'IV', 'oral', 'IM', 'IV + oral', 'IM + IV'
Use 'IV + oral' when the regimen transitions from intravenous to oral administration within the same course
Use 'IM + IV' only when both intramuscular and intravenous routes are used (not a transition to oral)
Do not infer route from drug class alone; it must be stated or clearly implied in the source text
Use 'NR' if the route of administration is not reported anywhere in the paper
subform_fields.field_description: Route of administration. Use 'IV + oral' for a regimen that switches from IV to oral mid-course; 'IM + IV' for a regimen given both intramuscularly and intravenously; 'IM' for intramuscular only.

hints: Look in the methods section under 'antibiotic regimen', 'dosing schedule', or the intervention arm description for the identified arm
Frequency is often embedded in the dose description (e.g., '500 mg every 8 h') — extract only the interval/schedule portion, leaving the dose amount and route to the `dose` field
For single-dose arms (e.g., single preoperative dose), 'single dose' is the appropriate frequency
If different frequencies apply to different phases (e.g., intra-operative vs. post-operative), capture both in order separated by 'then'
rules: Capture only the dosing interval or schedule — do NOT repeat the dose amount, units, or route (those belong in the `dose` field)
Use standard shorthand when the paper uses it (e.g., 'q8h', 'TID', 'every 8 hours') — transcribe as stated, condensed
For multi-phase regimens, join phase-specific intervals in administration order with 'then' (e.g., 'q4h intra-op then q6h oral')
Use 'single dose' for single-dose arms regardless of timing
Use 'NR' if the dosing interval or schedule is not stated in the paper
subform_fields.field_description: Dosing interval / schedule as the paper states it, condensed. Examples: 'every 8 hours', 'q4h intra-op then q6h oral', 'single dose'. Capture only the interval/schedule, not the full dose text. Use 'NR' if not stated.

hints: Look in the Methods section under 'antibiotic regimen', 'prophylaxis protocol', or 'treatment schedule' for the total course length
Check the dose field (already extracted) for embedded duration clues, but report only the total span here, not individual dose timings
For single-dose arms, confirm no post-operative doses are given before recording 'single dose'
For arms described as 'perioperative' or 'intraoperative only', infer duration as 'single dose' or the stated intraoperative window
If the paper states a range (e.g., '3–5 days'), record the range as given
rules: Report the total calendar duration of antibiotic administration for this arm, not the dosing interval or frequency (those belong in the 'frequency' field)
Use plain English with units: e.g., '5 days', '24 hours', '48 hours', 'single dose'
For a single pre-incision dose with no further doses, use 'single dose'
Do not include any post-antibiotic placebo period in the duration unless the paper explicitly bundles it (in that case append in parentheses, e.g., '1 day (placebo after)')
Use 'NR' if the total duration is not explicitly or inferably stated in the paper
subform_fields.field_description: Total duration of the regimen. Examples: '5 days', 'single dose', '24 hours', '1 day (placebo after)'. Use 'NR' if not stated.

hints: Check the CONSORT flow diagram first — it typically shows the number randomised to each arm as a box labelled 'Allocated to [arm name] (n = X)'
Look in the baseline characteristics table, which often has a column per arm with the randomised N in the header or first row
Check the randomisation or participant flow section of the Methods/Results text for phrases like 'X patients were randomised to...' or 'the [arm] group comprised X participants'
If the paper reports only the total randomised N and the number of arms, do not divide or infer — use 'NR' unless the per-arm figure is explicitly stated
This field captures the allocated (randomised) count, not the analysed, per-protocol, or ITT count — if only the analysed N is given and the allocated N is not stated, use 'NR'
rules: Must be a whole number (integer) representing participants allocated at randomisation
Do NOT use the number analysed at follow-up, the ITT population size, or the per-protocol population size unless the paper explicitly equates these to the randomised allocation count
Do NOT calculate or infer this value by subtraction or division from other reported figures; only record what is explicitly stated
Use "NR" if the per-arm randomised count is not explicitly reported in the paper
subform_fields.field_description: Number of participants allocated to THIS arm at randomisation (not the number analysed at follow-up). Look in the CONSORT flow diagram, randomisation table, or baseline characteristics table. Use 'NR' if not explicitly stated.

hints: Look in the methods section under 'allergy', 'hypersensitivity', 'penicillin allergy', or 'contraindications' subsections
Check footnotes of intervention tables or protocol descriptions for allergy-related substitution details
May appear as a parenthetical note alongside the primary regimen description, e.g. 'clindamycin was substituted for penicillin-allergic patients'
This field is distinct from the primary antibiotic_name, dose, route, frequency, and duration fields — capture only the allergy-specific substitute regimen here
rules: Quote the substitute drug (generic/INN name), dose with units, frequency, and duration in a single string, e.g. 'clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 h for 5 days'
Use 'None' if the paper does not describe any allergy substitution for this arm
Use 'NA' if the arm's primary antibiotic is already a non-beta-lactam (e.g. clindamycin, erythromycin, metronidazole) and an allergy substitution is therefore not applicable
Use 'NR' only if the paper explicitly mentions that an allergy substitution was used but does not provide the details
Do not repeat information already captured in antibiotic_name, dose, route, frequency, or duration unless it pertains specifically to the allergy-substitution regimen

examples.value: clindamycin 300 mg IV induction, 150 mg IV at 3 h, 150 mg PO every 6 h for 5 days

subform_fields.field_description: Substitute regimen administered to penicillin / beta-lactam-allergic participants in this arm. Quote the drug, dose, frequency, and duration. Use 'None' if no allergy substitution is described, 'NA' if the arm's primary antibiotic is already a non-beta-lactam (e.g. clindamycin).
